newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Anderton has qualms on Lab-NZ First fiscal stance.
newsitem.headline: Anderton has qualms on Lab-NZ First fiscal stance.

text.p: Alliance leader Jim Anderton said on Tuesday he had some qualms about fiscal policy under a proposed Labour-New Zealand First coalition.
"We have reservations," Anderton told reporters when asked about the fiscal position.

"We have a position of great concern, as you know, about the balance of payments. Over time, we shall see what the impacts are, we will be able to give our view because we are not part of the government."
The Alliance said earlier it would support a Labour-NZ First government if NZ First chooses Labour as its preferred partner.
The Alliance said a Labour-led government would discuss legislative initiatives with it in good faith.
Anderton said he believed New Zealand First leader Winston Peters and his party were serious about wanting to govern with Labour.
"This gives them the absolute authority to...without a blank cheque," he said.

The alternative, if New Zealand First chose the conservative National Party as its partner, was an unstable one or two-vote majority and reliance on support from radical free-market Act New Zealand, Anderton said.
NZ First was expected to announce its choice of coalition ally later on Tuesday, ending two months of deadlock since the October 12 general election.
